postings.description:
About Us

Beast Industries is a multifaceted media and entertainment company founded by Jimmy Donaldson, popularly known as MrBeast, the most watched person in the world. Renowned for revolutionizing digital content creation, Beast Industries encompasses a diverse portfolio of ventures that extend far beyond its origins on YouTube. With a mission to entertain, inspire, and create significant social impact, Beast Industries operates across various domains including digital media, philanthropy, consumer products, and innovative business initiatives. At Beast Industries, we believe in the transformative power of digital media and its potential to entertain, educate, and effect positive change. Our commitment to innovation, creativity, and philanthropy drives us to explore new frontiers, create unforgettable experiences, and build a legacy that inspires future generations.
About the Role

As the Account Director, Strategist, Agency at MrBeast, you are the senior strategist who owns the pre-sale phase of agency-sourced integrations in the MrBeast ecosystem. Your primary client is a holding-company agency team: media planners, integrated strategists, and activation leads at agencies (e.g.; Publicis, Omnicom, WPP, IPG, dentsu, or the independents), who are themselves servicing their own marketer clients.

You are the person they trust to bring MrBeast into their client's plan credibly, and the person who translates their client's brief into a MrBeast content architecture that survives both agency scrutiny and marketer approval.

This role is based in New York, where you’ll work in-office five days per week.

What You’ll Do

- Spearhead pre-sale strategies: craft compelling pitch decks, concept docs, KPI models, and custom pricing frameworks tailored to agency briefs.

- Navigate holding-company dynamics with agility, seamlessly adapting pitches to fit diverse RFP processes and agency workflows.

- Transform complex marketer goals into high-impact MrBeast content integration opportunities that exceed expectations.

- Design agency-ready packaging, including custom case studies, audience-sizing data, and flexible creative executions.

- Manage multiple high-priority accounts simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

- Deliver post-campaign insights, measurement snapshots, and pitch-ready anonymized wins to empower partners to win future campaigns with us.

What We’re Looking For

- 15+ years of experience in media-agency-side integrated marketing strategy, brand-side media planning, or platform and publisher partnerships focused on agency channels.

- Native holding-company literacy. You’ve worked at, sold into, or sourced from at least three of the major holding companies, and you know the difference between how GroupM approaches an RFP and how Omnicom Media Group does.

- A track record of packaging integrated campaigns for agency-sourced clients, either from the publisher side (network, streamer, platform sales) or from the agency side (media planning, integrated strategy).

- Media literacy. You should be able to specify what a MrBeast integration looks like without needing Production to explain it.

- Comfort operating in a higher-volume environment with multiple concurrent deals in motion.

Fixed annual salary of $178,000 - $223,000 plus an annual bonus, an employee equity plan grant, and comprehensive benefits.

Equity grants are issued in good faith, subject to company policies, board approval, and individual eligibility.

As the Account Director, Strategist, Financial Services at MrBeast, you are the senior strategist owning the pre-sale phase of every integration inside the MrBeast ecosystem for one of our largest financial services partners. Your job is to take the strategic direction set by the VP Partnerships and convert it into a specific, sellable concept that ties your client’s business objectives (product launches, account acquisition, new feature introductions) to MrBeast’s creative language and audience.

Your primary focus is high-level strategy and pre-sale development, allowing our dedicated production teams to manage execution and on-set activation.

This role is based in New York, where you’ll work in-office five days per week, or you’ll operate in a fully remote environment while maintaining tight, daily collaboration with teams in New York and North Carolina. Regardless of location, you’ll be expected to operate on Eastern Standard Time (EST) hours to stay aligned with headquarters, deal flow, and production timelines.

What You’ll Do

- Develop the pre-sale deliverable for every integration, including the concept doc, pitch deck, KPI mapping, and measurement architecture.

- Manage the partner content marketing calendar to ensure every product launch is packaged around a high-impact content moment.

- Translate the client’s business objectives into MrBeast content architecture. If the client is launching a new flagship product with a repositioning around a specific financial capability, you are the person who figures out whether that lands better as a Main Channel headline integration, a Shorts campaign, or a Beast Games challenge.

- Spearhead brand-KPI-to-asset mapping by aligning client measurement goals (such as unaided awareness lift, purchase consideration, app downloads, and account openings) with the optimal MrBeast assets.

- Collaborate with the Creative Lead on concept feasibility, production complexity, and creative fit with MrBeast’s brand voice. You are the strategic translator between the client’s brief and MrBeast’s studio.

- Build the acquisition-and-retention narrative into every integration, ensuring every proposal has a defensible answer to how it drives new funded accounts or reduces attrition.

- Manage regulated-category constraints in pre-sale, baking required disclosures, banking disclaimers, and compliant claims into the concept rather than into a post-approval fight.

- Coordinate with the client’s product and growth marketing teams, architecting the connection where a MrBeast integration ties to app onboarding or card activation.

- Lead the concept-to-close cycle as the primary quarterback of the pre-sale motion, from first client conversation to signed IO, with the VP staying consultative at the executive level.

- Hand off cleanly to Activation. When the deal closes, you brief the Activation Account Director comprehensively, then stay consultative through production, but you do not own execution.

- Feed learnings back into the strategy. After every activation, you incorporate what worked and what didn’t into the next cycle.

What We’re Looking For

- 15+ years of experience blending integrated marketing strategy with financial services account leadership, either brand-side or agency-side.

- Direct experience packaging integrated campaigns with a top-tier YouTuber, streaming platform, or premium content publisher.

- Product-marketing experience relevant to co-branded financial products. Anyone who has led a co-branded card, licensed-product, or merchandise marketing motion will translate cleanly.

- Working knowledge of financial marketing regulations and comfort partnering with client legal and compliance teams.

- Fluency in both worlds. You should be able to sit in a client marketing planning meeting and be treated as a peer, and sit in a MrBeast creative brainstorm and contribute meaningfully to the concept.

- Track record of KPI-mapping sophistication. You’ve built measurement frameworks that survived a marketing-mix modeling review.

- Media literacy sufficient to be conversant on production feasibility. You don’t need to be a producer, but you can’t propose concepts that are physically un-shootable.

- Consulting background welcome. MBB associates or engagement managers with a Financial Services expertise, or corporate development for financial services clients at a media firm, both translate cleanly.

Fixed annual salary of $178,000 - $223,000 plus an annual bonus, an employee equity plan grant, and comprehensive benefits.

Our teams move fast, think big, and take ownership. We chase ambitious ideas, execute relentlessly, and are building something that has never existed before. We are a uniquely multi-generational team of creators, operators, and builders across very different businesses, and we only win if everyone is connected to the same mission.

The Role

Beast Industries is growing quickly, and we need someone to own how our people understand our mission and goals, embrace the products and services we’re building (and the “why” behind them), get company information and stay connected to each other.. You'll build our internal communications function from scratch as a system, not a stream of tactics, so every employee understands where we're headed, sees how their work connects to the mission, and knows what's expected of them. You'll also make sure they hear about big changes from us, clearly and early, and in ways that are authentic to our culture. You'll work closely with executive leadership to build and carry the story of the company, translating strategy into a mission every employee can repeat in their own words. You'll connect teams across our businesses, our offices and remote employees, build trust in senior leadership, ensure no information gaps exist, and highlight the work our teams do every day.

You'll meet an employee audience that uses a mix of written, video, audio, live, and mobile formats daily, so our communications must be designed to meet them where they are. You're an excellent writer and a sharp advisor to executives. You have a strong point of view on how to communicate well, and you're just as eager to hear a better idea. You can make complicated things simple, stay honest and direct when the news is hard, and pair empathy with data to understand what's landing with employees. You reason from first principles: you ask what problem a message or channel is solving before choosing the format, then test, learn, and retire what doesn't work.

This role reports to the Chief Communications Officer and partners with the CEO, Chief People Officer, General Counsel, CFO, and business unit Presidents.

What You'll Do

Own Internal Communications

- Set the vision and strategy for internal communications across Beast Industries, and run it day to day.

- Define the mission narrative: the single story that connects company strategy, quarterly priorities, and each team's work, so any employee can answer "why does my work matter?"

- Create regular touchpoints, like all-hands and leadership updates, that employees can count on, on a published weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadence, with a clear standard for how quickly decisions are shared.

- Help executives communicate in their own voice while keeping messages consistent across the company.

- Build a manager cascade to equip people managers with the messaging, materials and context they need to ensure key announcements and people/HR related changes are communicated effectively throughout all levels of the organization. In success, this cascade will establish managers as one of our most trusted channels for information.

- Find and close information deserts: diagnose which teams, locations, tenure groups, and roles are consistently last to know, and fix the gaps.

- Design a multi-format channel strategy that considers audience preferences across business units and roles.

- Create two-way channels, including pulse surveys, and a visible "you said, we did" loop.

Partner with Executives

- Be a trusted advisor to senior executives and functional leaders.

- Draft CEO communications, including announcements, org updates, talking points, remarks, presentations, FAQs, and video scripts.

- Lead communications for tentpole, company-wide People team initiatives.

Build Culture

- Own leadership forums, AMAs, recognition programs, and engagement initiatives.

- Design the communications arc for new-hire onboarding and rapid growth, so every new employee feels connected to the mission from day one.

Measure What Works

- Set metrics for internal communications, track them consistently and share regularly with leadership.

- Use engagement data and employee feedback to improve our channels, cadence, and content.

- Run small, regular experiments on formats, timing, and channels; keep what works and retire what doesn't.

What We're Looking For

- 8+ years in internal communications, executive communications, change management, or a related field.

- Experience building or leading internal communications at a high-growth company.

- Outstanding writing, editing, and storytelling, across different audiences and formats.

- A track record advising executives and influencing senior stakeholders.

- Experience leading communications through growth, transformation, or organizational change.

- By Month 6: Internal narrative is live, baseline metrics are established and aligned on with leadership and companywide cadence of comms is being tested and refined. Launched an internal communications strategy and core programs that employees rely on.

- Became a trusted advisor to executive leadership on employee communications. Raised employee engagement with company communications and understanding of company priorities, with clear metrics to show it.

At Beast, communication is how we keep people connected to the mission and to each other. You'll build this function from the start, work directly with the leaders shaping the company's future, and help one of the fastest-growing entertainment companies in the world stay close as it grows. MrBeast makes some of the most watched content on the planet, and almost none of it happens in a normal office. Our IT team supported close to 30 productions in the first half of 2026 alone: building networks on sets that didn't exist a week earlier, running livestreams with dozens of simultaneous feeds, shipping custom hardware and software to shoots, and keeping a fleet of hundreds of loaner devices moving in and out of the field.

This role sits at the center of that work. You're an experienced technologist who is genuinely comfortable on a production set, and you're the person who brings order to studio support: you take a producer's idea, figure out what it actually needs from a technology standpoint, scope it into a technical solution roadmap, and either build it yourself or coordinate the teammates who will. When cameras roll, the tech works because you were in the room early.

This is not a helpdesk position. We have a support desk that handles day-to-day tickets; you're the layer above it. You'll carry engineering-level IT operations work between productions, act as an escalation point, and use AI aggressively to make yourself and the whole team faster.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Support productions on the ground. Design, deploy, and tear down networks for shoots at permanent studios and pop-up locations. Support AV and livestream rigs, on-site shoot tech, town halls and company events, and the loaner hardware fleet (laptops, phones, iPads, satellite internet) that keeps productions running.

- Scope production technology projects. Work our production intake process alongside the team that owns it. Sit in planning meetings with ideation, creation, and production, translate creative concepts into technical requirements, timelines, and budgets, and flag risks before they become night-before fires. - Coordinate the work, not just do it. Production support is shared across the whole IT team. You'll help decide who covers what shoot, keep documentation current so no project depends on one person's memory, and make sure every engagement gets a clean handoff and closeout.

- Carry engineering-level IT operations. Own projects across identity and access (Okta, Google Workspace), endpoint management and MDM rollouts (Mac and Windows), network infrastructure, and system integrations. Serve as an escalation point above the support desk and contribute to purchasing decisions and annual IT planning.

- Use AI like a power tool. We expect agentic AI in daily use here, not as a novelty. You'll build and maintain automations and agent workflows, contribute to our AI-assisted helpdesk, and prototype internal tools for production departments with AI assistance. If a task is repetitive, your instinct should be to automate it.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- 5+ years in hands-on IT, systems, or solutions engineering in a fast-moving environment, with strong fundamentals across identity, endpoints, networking, and troubleshooting under pressure.

- Real production or live-event experience. You've supported video production, broadcast, live streaming, staging, or live events, and you know what a set needs from technology before anyone asks.

- Solid networking chops. You can stand up a reliable temporary network (Wi-Fi, VLANs, firewalls, failover, DHCP/DNS/VPN) in an imperfect location on a deadline.

- Demonstrated agentic AI use. You've built something real with AI agents or automation platforms: workflows, integrations, internal tools. Chat-only usage doesn't count. Be ready to show us.

- An organizer's brain. You intake business requirements, scope work before starting it, write things down, and communicate clearly with non-technical creatives under stress.

- A strong security foundation. You build with data security, access control, and best practices in mind by default.

- Production-compatible flexibility. On-site in Greenville, NC, with shoot-driven hours and occasional travel. Productions don't keep office hours and neither does this role, though we work hard to keep the load sane and shared.

NICE TO HAVE

- Enterprise tooling we use: Okta, Google Workspace admin, Slack, MDM (FleetDM, Intune or similar), enterprise networking platforms (Meter, Ubiquiti, Cisco).

- Project coordination experience in a production, events, or MSP context where you owned scoping and client communication.

- Certifications (CompTIA A+/Network+, Google IT, Apple, Microsoft, Linux) are a plus, not a requirement. We care more about what you've built.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT

In the last year this team has built GPS trackers worn by contestants, custom weigh-in systems for a weight-loss show, networking for fifty simultaneous streamers, and biometrics for people surviving in the wilderness. Nobody sells an off-the-shelf product for most of what we're asked to do, which is exactly the fun of it. If you want an IT job where the requests are predictable, this is the wrong posting.
